items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: A friend of my wife and I, Colette Lacroix, had given Lily the phone number...

ctx.x: But the most important day of the month of October to me was the 8th. That was the day that Lily and I got married. And what a wild day that was. I had gotten my divorce and Lily also. As we were both foreigners in France, we had to run here and there to sign all sorts of papers until the last minute. As we were only staying in Paris for a short time, we had to get an exemption for publication of banms.

This was going to be a strictly private affair. People were believing that we were married already. We had invited only a couple of good friends, Maurice and Vonette Cullaz and Colette Lacroix and a French guy, Sacha Dillot. Sacha was best man and Colette the brides maid. The civil marriage was to be performed at the Town Hall (Mairie St.Sulpice) of the 6th district, which was the district where we lived whenever we were in Paris. A religious ceremony was to take place after at 6 o'clock at the American Church.…

Louis Lamy, the owner of the bus we had hired, came to see us about lunch time, then somebody else and about 4 a.m. "Bish" came in our hotel room and started to tell us some story. We were nervous and finally had to push him our of the room, telling him: "Bish, we have got to get dressed, because we are going to get married...." If we would not have been in such a hurry, it would have been comic to see his face!
